params.body:
## Why

Shane tried the unknown-chassis dialog on staging: *"maar wel raar corrigeren en klopt op deze"*. He is right, and the reason is structural.

The dialog showed the mileage and the chassis number as **editable fields**, with three buttons underneath: *Nee* / *VIN corrigeren* / *VIN klopt*. With inputs on screen, both of those buttons act on the same two values, so nothing on screen tells the dealer which button decides what. The old jQuery code papered over it by comparing the submitted values with the ones sent to Car-Pass and silently turning a confirmation into a correction whenever a field had been touched. Clever, invisible, and therefore not something a user can rely on: the only signal separating "confirm" from "correct" was one the dealer could not see.

This matters here more than in an ordinary form. A confirmation registers the mileage under that chassis number in a public register, dated today, and it can only be done the same day.

## What it is now

**Step 1 — the question.** The mileage and the chassis number stand there as text, formatted the way the confirmation before a request formats them (thousands separated). One question: is this number right?

- *Nummer klopt* (primary) — sends a `confirm`, carrying no values at all.
- *Nummer aanpassen* — opens step 2.
- *Nee* — closes, sends nothing.

The explanatory paragraph stays and gained a line: the reading shown is the one that will be registered under today's date, in a public register, so it is worth a second look. It still promises nothing we cannot back — no claim that Car-Pass creates the vehicle (V-19), and no billing claim (V-20, removed in PR 312).

**Step 2 — after *Nummer aanpassen*.** The same two values, now as prefilled fields, with *Correctie versturen* as the only primary button. *Terug* returns to step 1 rather than closing the dialog: "aanpassen" is a detour off one question, and whoever abandons the detour is back at the question. Step 1 is where you leave, via *Nee*.

So what is sent follows from the button that was pressed.

## The mileage field

It stays, and it stays editable in step 2. Car-Pass issue 131 is about the VIN, so the question was fair, but the mileage is not a leftover from the old one-size-fits-all dialog: it is the value that actually gets written, as `odometerReading` with today's date. A dealer who notices at this exact moment that the reading is wrong should be able to fix it here. Making them cancel, walk to the vehicle sheet, correct it and start over is worse, and it invites confirming the wrong number instead. The general correction dialog (the one titled with Car-Pass's own message, R S3-2.20) is untouched and keeps both fields as well.

## The invisible comparison

It survives as a **server-side safety net only**. A confirmation arriving with values that differ from what was sent to Car-Pass still becomes a correction, because confirming says "what you received is right" and that cannot be true of a number that has just changed. It is no longer the only thing standing between the two outcomes; step 1 sends no values, so the button decides. The tests that pin the guard stay, re-documented as what it now is.

## Rules, tests, screenshots

- R S3-2.17 rewritten around the two steps; R S3-2.21 rewritten around the guard as a safety net.
- New finding **X-95**: at an unknown chassis number there is exactly one obvious primary action at any moment.
- `92-testdekking.md` and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html` regenerated (`bin/rules-coverage --write`, `bin/rules-page`); the coverage table is unchanged because no rules were added or removed, only reworded.
- `CarpassRequestFeedbackTest` extended: step 1 carries the numbers as text and no input; step 2 carries the two fields; *Nummer klopt* sends a confirm without values; *Correctie versturen* with a changed chassis sends a correction with the new value; step 2 can correct the mileage too; cancelling sends nothing. No outbound call: the controller is a stand-in, the Outbound seal is never consulted.
- Labels: `confirm_vin` → "Nummer klopt", `correct_vin` → "Nummer aanpassen", new `send_correction` → "Correctie versturen", and `unknown_vin_prompt` rewritten. All five languages.
- Verified locally: `OwnStockList|Carpass|CarPass|RulesCoverage|StylesheetSyntax|BuildContract|SmokeTest` — 206 tests, 1063 assertions, green.
params.title: Unknown chassis number: one clear action at a time
